tcoSource:
5-year totals at 15,000 mi/yr.

**Primary source — depreciation:** [Recharged: Volvo EX30 Value After 5 Years](https://recharged.com/articles/volvo-ex30-value-after-5-years) (drawing on KBB/Edmunds residuals) — 2025 EX30 Twin Motor Performance Plus depreciates `$30,527` over 5 years, residual `$15,668`. KBB's 5-year cost-to-own for this trim is `$64,455`.

**Other line items (scaled from [Edmunds 2026 Volvo EX30 TCO](https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/ex30/2026/cost-to-own/) reference at MSRP `$47,258`, applied to AWD MSRP `$44,900`):**
- Insurance: Edmunds avg `$12,240` — similar across trims.
- Fuel: scaled for lower AWD efficiency (~98 MPGe vs Single Motor 117 MPGe) → `$2,500`.
- Maintenance `$2,000` + Repairs `$1,000` per [Recharged](https://recharged.com/articles/volvo-ex30-true-cost-of-ownership-5-years) `$3,000` 5-yr maint+repair estimate (Twin Motor slightly heavier wear than RWD).
- Financing: `$7,378 × (44,900 / 47,258)` ≈ `$7,010`.
- Taxes & fees: ~8% of MSRP → `$3,600`.

**Reconciliation:** Sum of itemized lines `$58,877` vs KBB `$64,455` aggregate — `$5,578` gap likely opportunity-cost or higher state tax assumptions in KBB's model.

title: Twin Motor Performance Ultra
infotainment: 12.3-inch portrait center display, Volvo Car UX on Android Automotive OS with Google Built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store)
adasStandard: Volvo's standard suite includes forward collision warning with auto-emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, driver attention/drowsiness monitoring, road-sign recognition, and a 360-degree camera. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/ex30-electric/specifications/
adasOptional: Pilot Assist (Volvo's hands-on Level 2 highway driving assistant — adaptive cruise + lane centering + automated lane changes up to 80 mph) is included on Ultra trim and available as a $499–$595 OTA download on lower trims for cars with Google Built-in. Source: https://www.swedespeed.com/threads/pilot-assist-now-available-as-a-downloadable-software-upgrade-for-499.695699/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view camera with dynamic guidelines. Resolution is HD. Integrated into the 12.3-inch portrait center display.
sideViewCameraNotes: Standard 360-degree surround-view camera on the Ultra trim. No dedicated side-blind camera (Honda LaneWatch-style); side awareness is via blind-spot monitor and surround-view.
subscriptionFeatures: Google services subscription after the first 4 years (Maps/Assistant/Play). Pilot Assist is a $499–$595 one-time OTA purchase on cars where it isn't standard. No heated-seat / performance-on-demand subscriptions on the EX30. Source: https://www.swedespeed.com/threads/pilot-assist-now-available-as-a-downloadable-software-upgrade-for-499.695699/
drmNotes: Core driving works offline. Volvo Car UX with Google Built-in: Google Maps, Google Assistant, Play Store, OTA software updates, and Volvo Cars app remote features (lock/unlock, climate preconditioning, charge scheduling, locate) all require connectivity. Four years of complimentary Google services included; renewal required after that. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/topic/56b126a04cecae0fc0a8015133ca61ef/
killSwitchNotes: No federal impaired-driving kill switch deployed on the EX30. The EX30 has driver attention monitoring (drowsiness/distraction warnings via the cabin camera) but does not include the more advanced interior-sensing impairment-detection system that ships on the EX90. No automatic vehicle stoppage based on impairment detection.
knownIssues: Early infotainment freezes and digital-key glitches reported by Twin Motor Performance owners — addressed by 2025 OTA waves. Touch-only controls (no physical buttons for HVAC, mirrors, etc.) consistently flagged as a usability problem. Sources: https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-volvo-ex30-twin-motor-performance-ultra-fashionable-but-late/
recalls: Data unavailable: NHTSA recall search for MY2025 EX30 did not surface major recalls as of 2026-05; the EX30 is a low-volume US vehicle with limited recall history. Verify at https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls before purchase.
stateIncentives: State EV incentives still apply (CA CVRP/CVAP, CO state rebate, NY Drive Clean, NJ ZEV sales-tax exemption, etc.) but the federal $7,500 credit ended Sept 30, 2025 and the Belgium-built EX30 was not assembled in North America, so it would have been excluded from full-credit eligibility even before the sunset. Source: https://www.edmunds.com/fuel-economy/the-ins-and-outs-of-electric-vehicle-tax-credits.html
tcoSource: Hybrid KBB + Edmunds/CarEdge. KBB 5-Year Cost to Own for 2025 Volvo EX30 Twin Motor Performance Ultra: total $62,854; depreciation $32,489; out-of-pocket $30,365 (https://www.kbb.com/volvo/ex30/2025/twin-motor-performance-ultra/, retrieved 2026-05-21). Edmunds True Cost to Own® page (https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/ex30/2025/cost-to-own/, summarized via CarEdge https://caredge.com/volvo/ex30/costs) publishes EX30 averages: fuel $2,120, insurance $12,240, maintenance+repairs $2,232, financing $7,378. Edmunds component breakdown used directly; combined maint+repairs split 75/25 (typical EV ratio). Residual $30,365 - $23,970 = $6,395 attributed to taxes & fees. EX30 US delivery launched late; Edmunds does not yet publish a per-trim split, so EX30-wide averages are used and the depreciation/total reflect the Twin Motor Performance Ultra trim specifically per KBB.

title: Twin Motor Plus
exclusionReason: Has kill switch (interior-sensing impairment-detection system can stop the vehicle)
infotainment: 14.5-inch portrait center display, Volvo Car UX on Android Automotive OS, Google Built-in, 11.2-inch digital instrument cluster
adasStandard: EX90 ships with Volvo's full standard suite plus interior-sensing driver-monitoring system (cabin camera + capacitive steering wheel) for impairment/drowsiness/distraction detection. Pilot Assist (L2 highway), 360-degree camera, blind-spot, rear cross-traffic, AEB front/rear. LiDAR is included as hardware in all EX90s for future advanced ADAS but is not currently driving any released features in the US. Source: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/ex90-electric/specifications/
adasOptional: More advanced ADAS features (incl. eventual hands-free highway assist) planned via OTA on the LiDAR-equipped hardware. As of 2026-05 not all promised features are released. Source: https://recharged.com/articles/volvo-ex90-software-update-history
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard HD rear-view camera with dynamic guidelines, integrated into the 14.5-inch center display.
sideViewCameraNotes: Standard 360-degree surround-view camera. No dedicated side-blind camera.
subscriptionFeatures: Google services included for 4 years, subscription renewal after. Pilot Assist standard on EX90. Bidirectional charging promised as future OTA. Source: https://www.swedespeed.com/threads/pilot-assist-now-available-as-a-downloadable-software-upgrade-for-499.695699/
drmNotes: EX90's launch software was notably incomplete — wireless CarPlay, full Pilot Assist, bidirectional charging marketing all shipped disabled and were rolled out via OTA waves through 2025. This OTA gating is precedent for Volvo using connectivity as a feature-delivery and feature-control mechanism. Sources: https://insideevs.com/news/781786/volvo-aaos-update-delay/, https://recharged.com/articles/volvo-ex90-software-update-history
killSwitchNotes: EX90 carries Volvo's interior-sensing system: cabin camera detects gaze direction / eye closure, capacitive steering-wheel sensor detects hands-off. On detection of impairment (drowsiness, distraction, sustained inattention), the system escalates from gentle nudge to persistent alert to (per Volvo's stated capability) safely slowing the car to a stop with hazards activated. Volvo publicly positions this as their answer to the federal impaired-driving-detection mandate (IIJA). The system is not user-disableable and is software/hardware integrated — not a separate hardware kill switch but an in-vehicle decision system that can take control. Sources: https://www.automotive-fleet.com/10182151/volvo-driver-sensing-system-aims-to-reduce-distracted-drowsy-driving-crashes, https://www.autocar.co.uk/car-news/new-cars/volvo-ex90
knownIssues: Documented software issues at launch: infotainment freezes, intermittent digital-key failures, missing features that required multiple OTA waves to enable. Hardware build quality solid; software the major friction. 400V architecture limits charging speeds vs. 800V competitors. Source: https://recharged.com/articles/2024-volvo-ex90-problems-and-fixes
recalls: EX90 has had several NHTSA recalls in 2024-2025 covering software issues; check https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls for current state.
stateIncentives: EX90 is assembled in Ridgeville, SC and most trims fall under the $80k MSRP cap, so MY2025 EX90 qualified for the full $7,500 federal credit through Sept 30, 2025 (when the credit sunsetted under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act). State incentives still apply per state. Sources: https://www.greencarreports.com/news/1141599_us-made-2025-volvo-ex90-price-tax-credit, https://www.edmunds.com/fuel-economy/the-ins-and-outs-of-electric-vehicle-tax-credits.html
